name: Section
summary: An edge-to-edge band of a website page, with its own surface, site spacing and, optionally, its own theme. variant="footer" makes it the site's footer; variant="hero" makes it the page opening.

a11y.apg: A <section> element. It is only announced as a region (a landmark) when it has an accessible name, so give the band a heading and point aria-labelledby at it when screen-reader users should be able to jump to it. No keyboard interaction: it is a layout band. With variant="footer" it is a <footer>, which is the page's contentinfo landmark when it is not nested in another sectioning element; its links sit in a <nav> named by `navLabel`, each column under an <h2>. With variant="hero" it is a <section> whose title is the page's <h1> (titleAs="h2" when it is not the first band); point aria-labelledby at the title to list it as a region.

props.name: surface
props.description: The band's background: the page's (the default), a card surface, or the recessed inset surface.

props.name: spacing
props.description: The space above and below: md is --space-16 (64) and --space-24 (96) from the md breakpoint up; sm is half of that. Aurea's choice from existing tokens: none of the references had a section to read.

props.name: theme
props.description: A theme for this band only: theme="dark" makes a dark band inside a light page, and the other way round. The background, the text and every piece inside follow the band's theme, and the page's light-theme rules do not leak into it.

props.name: variant
props.description: footer makes the band the website's footer: a <footer> with the brand, the link columns and the legal line, its content already in a Container. Surface, spacing and theme keep working — a dark footer on a light page is theme="dark". On a phone everything stacks in one column. `hero` is the opening of a page: eyebrow, title, text, buttons or an e-mail field, and an image beside them; on a phone, everything stacks.

props.name: brand
props.description: Footer only: the brand and a short line, top left.

props.name: links
props.description: Footer only: the link columns, each { title, items }. The items are SidebarItem (id, label, href, render), the same shape as the menus. From 768px the columns share the width, each at least 8rem.

props.name: legal
props.description: Footer only: the bottom line — rights, terms, privacy — under a hairline.

props.name: layout
props.description: Only on footer: columns is the large site footer; inline is ONE centred line, as the reference's home page footer — the legal sentence, the links (without the column titles) and the children (social icons). The brand does not go in.

props.name: maxWidth
props.description: Footer only: how far the content grows, on the Container's scale.

props.name: navLabel
props.description: Footer only: the footer navigation's name for screen readers. Pass it in the page's language.

props.name: title
props.description: Only on hero: the title of the opening, the page's h1. It grows with the width of the BAND, not of the window: --text-4xl (36), --text-6xl (60) from 768 and --text-7xl (72) from 1024. On the other variants a string here is still the HTML title attribute.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: Only on hero: the tag of the title. The opening is the start of the page, so h1; h2 when the band opens a section further down.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Only on hero: the line above the title — a badge, a short phrase, a link to what changed. 8 above the title, 16 from 1024.

props.name: description
props.description: Only on hero: the text under the title, glued to it. 16/24, and 18/28 from 768, at most 672 wide.

props.name: actions
props.description: Only on hero: the buttons, or a form with the e-mail field and its button (the form grows up to 480). 16 under the text.

props.name: media
props.description: Only on hero: the image, or the piece that proves what the text says. With align="start" it sits beside the text from 1024 and under it before that. It takes the width of its column: size a phone frame in the app.

props.name: align
props.description: Only on hero: start puts the text on the left and the image beside it; center puts everything on the middle line, with the image under the text. What comes as children goes after the buttons.

props.name: children
props.description: The band's content, usually inside a Container.
